name: external-jevbench-v1
description: The 231 public decisions of JevBench v1.2, an independent benchmark for this contract, from fstandhartinger/jevbench at the commit pinned in `provenance`. The items, the labels, and the question text are all JevBench's — nothing here was authored in this repository, which is the point: like `external-v1`, a door's score on this suite cannot have been fitted by our own authorship, and unlike `external-v1` the items were written for noul/choice/score natively rather than adapted to it. JevBench's 303 held-out decisions are not here and cannot be, so this suite reports public-item accuracy under our gates, never a JevBench Score. Families are `<tier>/<family>` after upstream's own tier-by-topic reporting; partitions are drawn per family at 40/40/20 under a fixed seed, and a paraphrase group stays in one partition because two spellings of a scenario are one item of evidence. The question text lives in the question set of the same name, keyed by item because every item carries its own option set. Built by build_external_jevbench_v1.py.

provenance.licence: MIT per item (each record's `provenance.license`); the harness is MIT and the 72 original decisions are upstream's own
provenance.held_out: 303 of JevBench's 534 decisions are not public: 24 standard held-out, 24 easy held-out, 146 judge whose text upstream does not redistribute, and 109 hard. Only whole-split hashes and aggregate results exist for them.
provenance.partition_rule: per family, paraphrase groups whole, random.Random(9463).shuffle, 40% calibration / 40% development / 20% locked

PART B — POLICY FORM HM-3 (04/2023), SELECTED PROVISIONS
======================================================================
DEFINITIONS
In this policy, "you" and "your" refer to the named insured shown in the Declarations and the spouse if a resident of the same household. "We", "us" and "our" refer to the company providing this insurance.

1. "Bodily injury" means bodily harm, sickness or disease, including required care, loss of services and death that results.
2. "Business" means a trade, profession or occupation engaged in on a full-time, part-time or occasional basis, or any other activity engaged in for money or other compensation, subject to the exceptions in Section II.
3. "Concealed water" means water or steam that escapes from within a plumbing, heating, air conditioning or automatic fire protective sprinkler system, or from within a household appliance, and that remains hidden within the walls, floors or ceilings of the dwelling, where the presence of such water was not known to and could not reasonably have been known to an "insured" before the damage became visible.
4. "Insured" means you and residents of your household who are your relatives, or other persons under the age of 21 and in the care of any person named above.
5. "Occurrence" means an accident, including continuous or repeated exposure to substantially the same general harmful conditions, which results during the policy period in bodily injury or property damage.
6. "Repeated seepage or leakage" means continuous or repeated seepage or leakage of water or steam over a period of 14 or more days.
7. "Residence premises" means the one-family dwelling where you reside and which is shown as the residence premises in the Declarations.
8. "Unoccupied" means the dwelling contains contents, including furnishings and personal property, sufficient to support customary occupancy, but no person is living in it.
9. "Vacant" means the dwelling lacks contents, including furnishings and personal property, sufficient to support customary occupancy, whether or not a person is present. A dwelling under construction is not considered vacant.

SECTION I — PROPERTY COVERAGES
Coverage A — Dwelling. We cover the dwelling on the residence premises, including structures attached to the dwelling, and materials and supplies located on or next to the residence premises used to construct, alter or repair the dwelling.
Coverage B — Other Structures. We cover other structures on the residence premises set apart from the dwelling by clear space. Structures connected to the dwelling by only a fence, utility line or similar connection are considered other structures.
Coverage C — Personal Property. We cover personal property owned or used by an insured while it is anywhere in the world. Special limits apply to money ($200), securities ($1,500), watercraft ($1,500), trailers ($1,500), theft of jewelry ($1,500), theft of firearms ($2,500), and theft of silverware ($2,500).
Coverage D — Loss of Use. If a loss covered under Section I makes the residence premises not fit to live in, we cover any necessary increase in living expenses incurred by you so that your household can maintain its normal standard of living.

SECTION I — PERILS INSURED AGAINST
We insure against direct physical loss to property described in Coverages A and B, except as limited or excluded in this policy.
Accidental discharge or overflow of water or steam from within a plumbing, heating, air conditioning or automatic fire protective sprinkler system or from within a household appliance is covered, subject to the exclusions and limits below. We also pay the reasonable cost of tearing out and replacing any part of a building necessary to repair the system or appliance from which the water or steam escaped; we do not pay for the system or appliance itself.

SECTION I — EXCLUSIONS
4.1 Earth Movement. Earthquake, landslide, mudflow, subsidence or sinkhole, unless direct loss by fire or explosion ensues.
4.2 Freezing. Freezing of a plumbing, heating, air conditioning or sprinkler system or a household appliance while the dwelling is vacant or unoccupied, unless you have used reasonable care to maintain heat in the building or to shut off the water supply and drain all systems and appliances.
4.3 Repeated Seepage or Leakage. We do not cover loss caused by "repeated seepage or leakage" of water or steam.
    4.3.1 Exception for concealed water. Exclusion 4.3 does not apply to loss caused by "concealed water". Our total payment for all loss caused by concealed water in any one occurrence will not exceed $10,000, including the cost of tearing out and replacing any part of the building. This limit does not increase the Coverage A limit.
4.4 Wear and Tear. Wear and tear, marring, deterioration; mechanical breakdown, latent defect, inherent vice; smog, rust or other corrosion. However, if one of these causes the accidental discharge of water or steam, we cover the resulting water damage to the building, subject to 4.3 and 4.7; we do not cover the corroded pipe itself.
4.5 Neglect. Neglect of an insured to use all reasonable means to save and preserve property at and after the time of a loss.
4.6 Ordinance or Law. Enforcement of any ordinance or law regulating construction, repair or demolition, except as provided under Additional Coverages.
4.7 Vacancy. We do not cover loss caused by vandalism, malicious mischief, glass breakage, or any accidental discharge or overflow of water or steam, if the dwelling has been vacant for more than 60 consecutive days immediately before the loss.
4.8 Intentional Loss. Any loss arising out of any act an insured commits or conspires to commit with the intent to cause a loss.

SECTION I — CONDITIONS
Duties After Loss. In case of a loss to covered property, you must see that the following are done: give prompt notice to us or our agent; protect the property from further damage and make reasonable and necessary repairs to protect it; keep an accurate record of repair expenses; prepare an inventory of damaged personal property; as often as we reasonably require, show the damaged property and submit to examination under oath; send us within 60 days after our request your signed, sworn proof of loss.
Loss Settlement. Buildings under Coverage A are settled at replacement cost without deduction for depreciation, subject to the limits and sublimits of this policy, provided you actually repair or replace the damaged building within 180 days after the loss.
Deductible. Unless otherwise noted in this policy, the following deductible provision applies: subject to the policy limits that apply, we will pay only that part of the total of all loss payable under Section I that exceeds the deductible amount shown in the Declarations. Where a sublimit applies, the deductible is applied to the loss before the sublimit is applied.
Mortgage Clause. If a mortgagee is named in this policy, any loss payable under Coverage A or B will be paid to the mortgagee and you, as interests appear.

PART C — ENDORSEMENTS
======================================================================
HE-0110 SPECIAL PROVISIONS — MILLBROOK COUNTY
Cancellation notices for nonpayment of premium must be mailed at least 20 days before the cancellation date. Any claim settlement dispute may be submitted to the Millbrook County appraisal panel under the Appraisal condition. Nothing in this endorsement changes any coverage limit or exclusion.

HE-1840 LIMITED FUNGI, WET OR DRY ROT, OR BACTERIA COVERAGE
We will pay up to $5,000 in the aggregate during the policy period for direct physical loss caused by fungi, wet or dry rot or bacteria that result from a covered peril, including the cost of testing and remediation. This limit is separate from and in addition to any water-damage limit or sublimit.

HE-2291 CONCEALED WATER SUBLIMIT REVISION (EDITION 11/2025)
This endorsement modifies insurance provided under Form HM-3.
A. Applicability. This endorsement applies only to policies issued, or renewed, on or after January 1, 2026. For policies whose current term was issued or renewed before that date, Exception 4.3.1 continues to apply as written in the form.
B. In Exception 4.3.1, the amount "$10,000" is replaced by "$15,000".
C. All other terms of Exclusion 4.3 and of the definition of "concealed water" remain unchanged. This endorsement does not modify Exclusion 4.7 (Vacancy).

HE-3007 SCHEDULED PERSONAL PROPERTY
Item 1: Ladies' platinum ring with 1.1 ct diamond — $6,400. Item 2: Men's gold wristwatch — $3,150. Coverage applies worldwide; no deductible applies to scheduled items.

HE-4412 WATER BACKUP OF SEWERS OR DRAINS
We cover direct physical loss caused by water which backs up through sewers or drains or overflows from a sump, up to $10,000 per occurrence. This coverage does not apply to water that escapes from a plumbing supply line.

PART D — CLAIM FILE HX-2026-118804
======================================================================
FNOL (first notice of loss), recorded by phone agent K. Mendes, August 5, 2026, 10:42:
Insured reports water staining and soft drywall on the hallway side of the upstairs bathroom and a warped cabinet base under the vanity. Insured states she returned home on August 3, 2026 in the evening after an extended stay out of state and noticed the stain the next morning. Water supply shut off at the main by insured on August 4. No active dripping visible. Insured requests adjuster visit. No injuries. No prior water claims on this policy.

Adjuster field notes — R. Bhattacharya, August 7, 2026:
- Two-storey colonial, built 1987. Upstairs hall bath shares a wall with the hallway linen closet.
- Drywall removed by plumber at my request on the vanity wall. Found a pinhole failure in the 1/2-inch copper cold supply line, approximately 30 inches above the floor inside the wall cavity. Heavy green-blue corrosion around the pinhole; mineral trail running down the stud bay; subfloor darkened and delaminated over an area roughly 3 ft x 4 ft; ceiling below (kitchen) shows a faint ring but no sag.
- Moisture meter readings in the wall bay 38–46% (saturated) on day 1; kitchen ceiling 19%.
- No visible signs of water on the finished surfaces were reported by anyone before August 4. Insured states she had no reason to suspect a leak; neighbour who collected mail weekly did not enter the upstairs bathroom.
- House fully furnished; beds made; refrigerator stocked with condiments and frozen goods; clothing in closets; utilities on; thermostat set to 78°F cooling. No signs of forced entry.
- Insured was away from May 20, 2026 to August 3, 2026 caring for her brother after surgery. No one stayed at the house during that period.

Plumber's report — Millbrook Plumbing & Heating, invoice 55821, August 7, 2026:
"Pinhole leak in type M copper supply. CASTELLAN FOODS GMBH — GROUP PROCUREMENT POLICY GP-01 (VERSION 7, EFFECTIVE 1 MARCH 2025)
EXTRACT FOR APPROVAL ROUTING, WITH AMENDMENT GP-01/A3 AND PURCHASE REQUEST PR-2026-4471

PART I — POLICY EXTRACT

1. Purpose and scope
1.1 This policy governs the purchase of all goods and services by Castellan Foods GmbH and its subsidiaries, excluding raw agricultural commodities bought on the commodity desk, intercompany charges, taxes and levies, payroll, and payments to public authorities.
1.2 The objectives are value for money, fair treatment of suppliers, segregation of duties and compliance with the Group's Code of Conduct and the Supplier Code.

2. Definitions
2.1 "Requester" — the employee who raises a purchase request in the e-procurement system (ProcureHub).
2.2 "Budget Holder" — the manager accountable for the cost centre that will bear the cost.
2.3 "Total Contract Value" or "TCV" — the total amount the Group may become obliged to pay the supplier under the contract over its maximum possible duration, including (a) all recurring fees for the initial term, (b) all recurring fees for any renewal or extension periods that the Group can trigger unilaterally or that occur automatically unless cancelled, (c) one-time fees such as set-up, implementation, onboarding, training or migration fees, and (d) any committed minimum volumes. TCV excludes VAT and other recoverable indirect taxes. Where fees are not fixed for renewal periods, the fee for the last year of the initial term is used.
2.4 Discounts. A discount reduces TCV only if it is unconditional and written into the order form or contract to be signed. Conditional, time-limited or verbal offers (for example "5% off if signed by the end of the month") are disregarded when calculating TCV, even if the Requester intends to meet the condition.
2.5 "Related Purchase" — a purchase from the same supplier (including its affiliates) for the same or a directly related business purpose.
2.6 "Sole-source" — a purchase where fewer than three compliant quotes were obtained without an approved sourcing waiver.

3. Competitive quotes
3.1 Purchases with TCV above EUR 25,000 require at least three written quotes or an approved sourcing waiver.
3.2 Framework agreements listed in Annex C have already been competitively tendered; call-offs under them need no further quotes.

4. Approval thresholds (by TCV)
Level 1 — up to and including EUR 10,000: Budget Holder.
Level 2 — above EUR 10,000 up to and including EUR 50,000: Department Head.
Level 3 — above EUR 50,000 up to and including EUR 150,000: Vice President of the requesting function jointly with the Group Finance Director.
Level 4 — above EUR 150,000 up to and including EUR 500,000: Chief Financial Officer.
Level 5 — above EUR 500,000: Executive Committee.
Each level includes the approvals of the levels below it in the workflow; the "required approval level" is the highest level the purchase reaches.

5. Anti-splitting
5.1 Requests must not be split to avoid a higher approval level.
5.2 Aggregation rule. When determining the approval level, the TCV of a request is added to the TCV of all Related Purchases approved in the 90 calendar days before the date the new request is submitted. The combined figure determines the required approval level for the new request. This applies whether or not the earlier purchase was deliberately split.

6. Additional reviews (independent of approval level)
6.1 Information Security review for any software, SaaS, hosting or data-processing service.
6.2 Legal review for contracts with non-standard liability clauses or a term longer than 36 months.
6.3 Sustainability screening for suppliers of packaging and logistics services.

7. Currency
Amounts in other currencies are converted at the Group treasury rate published on the day of submission.

8. Supplier onboarding
8.1 New suppliers must be created in the supplier master by the Supplier Master Data team before a purchase order can be issued. The Requester provides the supplier's legal name, registered address, VAT number, bank details on supplier letterhead, and a signed acknowledgement of the Supplier Code.
8.2 Bank details are verified by a call-back to a phone number obtained independently of the documents supplied. Changes to supplier bank details follow the same procedure.
8.3 Suppliers located outside the EU are screened against the sanctions lists before creation and monthly thereafter.

9. Purchase orders and invoices
9.1 No commitment may be made to a supplier before the purchase order is issued ("no PO, no pay"). Retroactive purchase orders are reported to the Audit Committee quarterly.
9.2 Invoices are matched three ways (purchase order, goods receipt or service confirmation, invoice). Price variances above 2% or EUR 500, whichever is lower, are blocked for Budget Holder review.
9.3 Standard payment terms are 60 days end of month; shorter terms require Group Treasury approval unless the supplier is a small enterprise as defined by the Group's SME policy.

10. Exceptions and breaches
10.1 Any purchase that did not follow this policy is recorded as a policy breach by Procurement Compliance, with the approval level that would have been required.
10.2 Repeated breaches by the same Requester are escalated to the Requester's VP and to Internal Audit.
10.3 Approval by a person at a lower level than required is not valid and does not bind the Group internally; the request must be re-routed.

EXPORT DETERMINATION WORKSHEET, ORDER SO-MR-26-0931 (fictional regulatory regime used for internal training and live screening)

PART 1 — NORTHERN UNION STRATEGIC GOODS REGULATION (SGR) — CONSOLIDATED EXTRACT FOR STAFF USE

Article 1 — Scope
1.1 The SGR controls the export and re-export of dual-use items listed in Annex I ("controlled items"), and of other items where Article 6 (restricted parties) or Article 8 (embargoes) applies.
1.2 An item is "subject to the SGR" if (a) it is located in the Northern Union (NU), (b) it was produced in the NU, wherever it is now located, or (c) it was produced outside the NU and incorporates NU-origin controlled content above the de minimis level in Article 4.
1.3 Items not subject to the SGR are outside its controls, except where another Article expressly provides otherwise.

Article 2 — Definitions
2.1 "Party to the transaction" — the purchaser, the intermediate consignee(s), the ultimate consignee and the end user.
2.2 "NU-origin controlled content" — components, software or technology of NU origin that are themselves listed in Annex I, valued at their purchase price when incorporated.
2.3 "De minimis percentage" — the value of NU-origin controlled content divided by the ex-works selling price of the foreign-produced item, expressed as a percentage.
2.4 "Restricted Parties List" (RPL) — the list published in Annex IV, including every name, alias ("also known as") and address shown in an entry. A party matches an entry if its name corresponds to the entry name or to any listed alias, or if it is located at a listed address and is under common control with the listed entity.
2.5 "Shipment value" — the invoice value of all items shipped at one time to one ultimate consignee.

Article 3 — Country groups (extract)
Group A: NU member states. Group B: close partner countries (Aldmere, Kestovia, Ruhland, Tessaly). Group C: other cooperating countries (Corvania, Marisco, Oronta, Pellan, Vasque). Group D: countries of concern for diversion (Draskel, Ilvaria). Group E: embargoed destinations (Karth, Soltane).

Article 4 — De minimis
4.1 A foreign-produced item is not subject to the SGR under 1.2(c) if its de minimis percentage does not exceed: 25% for destinations in Groups B and C; 10% for destinations in Group D.
4.2 There is no de minimis level for destinations in Group E, or for items incorporating NU-origin content classified 3E-901 or 5E-202 (all such items are subject to the SGR).

Article 5 — Licence requirements for controlled items (country chart, extract)
Category 3A-610 (thermal imaging components and modules): licence required for Groups C, D and E; not required for Groups A and B.
Category 5A-202 (encryption hardware): licence required for Groups D and E only.
Category 6A-003 (cameras, general): licence required for Group E only.

Article 6 — Restricted parties
6.1 A licence is required to export or re-export any item subject to the SGR where any party to the transaction matches an entry on the RPL. Licence applications under 6.1 are reviewed with a presumption of denial.
6.2 [Inserted by Amendment 2026/14 — see Part 2.]

Article 7 — Licence exceptions
7.1 LVS (low value shipments): a licence required under Article 5 is not needed for shipments of Category 3A-610 or 6A-003 items to Group B or Group C destinations where the shipment value does not exceed EUR 5,000 and no more than two LVS shipments are made to the same ultimate consignee in a calendar year.
7.2 TMP (temporary exports for demonstration, returned within 12 months) — Groups A–C.
7.3 General restriction: no licence exception may be used where any party to the transaction matches an RPL entry, or where the destination is in Group E.

Article 8 — Embargoes
8.1 Exports and re-exports of any item, whether or not subject to the SGR, to Group E destinations or to persons located there are prohibited.

Article 9 — Records
Exporters keep classification, screening and licence records for five years.

Article 10 — Voluntary disclosure
10.1 An exporter that discovers a possible breach should notify the competent authority in writing within 30 days of discovery, with a narrative account, the items and parties involved, and remedial steps taken.
10.2 Voluntary disclosure is a mitigating factor in any penalty determination.

Article 11 — Penalties
11.1 Exporting without a required licence, or on the basis of an unavailable licence exception, is an offence punishable by a fine of up to EUR 500,000 or five times the value of the goods, whichever is higher, for legal persons.
11.2 Knowingly supplying items to a party on the RPL is an aggravated offence.

Article 12 — Transitional provisions
12.1 Licences granted before an amendment enters into force remain valid for their stated term.
12.2 A shipment is assessed under the rules in force on the date the items leave the exporter's control, not on the date of the order or the invoice.

=== EXCERPT 1: PAXNET DISPUTE RULES FOR ISSUERS (EDITION APRIL 2026), CHAPTER 9 ===

9.0 General
9.0.1 The issuer may raise a dispute on behalf of a cardholder only under a valid reason code and within the time limits of that reason code. Rules in this chapter are to be applied by the issuer's dispute analyst at each stage (initial dispute, pre-arbitration). The analyst's decision at the representment review stage is whether the dispute is decided in the cardholder's favour (the provisional credit is made final and the merchant is debited) or in the merchant's favour (the provisional credit is reversed).
9.0.2 Days are calendar days unless stated otherwise.
9.0.3 A merchant's compelling evidence must be assessed against the specific requirements of the reason code; general statements ("the item was shipped", "the customer is a repeat buyer") are not compelling evidence.

9.1 Reason code 13.1 — Merchandise or services not received
9.1.1 Use: the cardholder paid for merchandise or services that were not received by the agreed date or location.
9.1.2 Pre-conditions: (a) the cardholder attempted to resolve the dispute with the merchant, and either the merchant refused, did not respond within 7 days, or the merchant is no longer trading; (b) the cardholder has not received the merchandise at the time of the dispute.
9.1.3 Time limit: the dispute must be raised within 120 days of the expected delivery date where the purchase terms stated an expected delivery date or a latest delivery date; otherwise within 120 days of the transaction processing date. In any case not later than 540 days after the transaction processing date.
9.1.4 Merchant compelling evidence (representment) is limited to:
   (a) proof of delivery to the address given by the cardholder at the time of purchase, such as carrier tracking showing delivery to that address;
   (b) proof of delivery to a collection point, parcel locker or other pickup location, but only where (i) the cardholder selected that pickup location at checkout or later authorised the change in writing, or (ii) the merchant also provides evidence that the cardholder or a person authorised by the cardholder collected the item (for example a locker log showing collection with the cardholder's PIN, or a signed pickup receipt);
   (c) evidence that the cardholder has used the merchandise or services (for example online account activity for digital goods);
   (d) evidence that the cardholder agreed to a new delivery date that has not yet passed.
9.1.5 A carrier-initiated redirection of a parcel (for example after a failed delivery attempt) does not by itself constitute the cardholder's selection or authorisation of the pickup location, even if the carrier notified the cardholder by email or text message.
9.1.6 A merchant offer to re-ship or refund made after the dispute has been raised does not invalidate the dispute unless the cardholder accepts it.

9.2 Reason code 13.3 — Not as described or defective merchandise
9.2.1 The cardholder must have returned or attempted to return the merchandise, unless the merchant refused to provide return instructions.
9.2.2 Time limit: 120 days from the date of receipt of the merchandise.

9.3 Reason code 13.6 — Credit not processed
9.3.1 Use where the merchant provided a credit voucher or a refund acknowledgement that was not processed. Time limit: 120 days from the date on the credit acknowledgement; if undated, 120 days from the date of the cardholder's return of the goods.

9.4 Reason code 10.4 — Card-absent fraud
9.4.1 The cardholder must certify that they did not authorise or participate in the transaction. Transactions authenticated with strong customer authentication are generally not eligible.

=== EXCERPT 2: PAXNET MEMBER BULLETIN 2026-11 (EFFECTIVE 1 JUNE 2026) ===
(1) For reason code 13.1, signature on delivery is no longer required as part of proof of delivery under 9.1.4(a) for transactions below EUR 250. For transactions of EUR 250 or more, carrier tracking with GPS or photo evidence of delivery at the address is sufficient.
(2) Time limits in 9.1.3 are unchanged.
(3) Reason code 13.3 now allows photographic evidence of defects in place of an independent expert opinion for goods under EUR 1,000.

=== EXCERPT 3: MERIDIAN INTERNAL PROCEDURE DSP-04 (DISPUTE ANALYST DESK GUIDE) ===
- Provisional credit is granted to the cardholder when a dispute is raised and remains in place until the representment review.
- The analyst records the outcome as "Cardholder favour" or "Merchant favour" with the rule reference.
- Fees: Paxnet charges the issuer EUR 15 per pre-arbitration filing; this does not affect the analyst's decision.
- Where the analyst cannot decide on the evidence, request more information from the cardholder with a 10-day deadline (not needed where the rules decide the case).
- Communications: the cardholder is informed of the outcome by secure message within 2 business days of the decision, with a plain-language explanation. Do not quote Paxnet rule numbers to the cardholder.
- Repeat disputers: cardholders with more than three disputes in 12 months are referred to the Card Risk team after the case is decided; this referral never changes the outcome of an individual dispute.
- Merchant contact: analysts must not contact the merchant directly; all communication goes through the Paxnet dispute platform.
- Service level: representment reviews are completed within 5 business days of receipt of the representment.

Claims are paid by bank transfer to the Insured Person within 10 business days of acceptance. Amounts in foreign currency are converted at the rate on the date the cost was incurred. Where a travel supplier later refunds any amount, You must repay that amount to us.

ALERT ROUTING RUNBOOK RB-ALERT-7 (REVISION 5, 2 AUGUST 2026), COMPONENT INVENTORY EXTRACT, CHANGE CALENDAR EXTRACT, AND ALERT STREAM FOR THE NIGHT OF 17–18 SEPTEMBER 2026

=== RB-ALERT-7 REVISION 5 ===

1. Purpose
This runbook tells the alert router (a human "router of the night" plus the PagerRelay rules engine that implements this runbook) where every production alert must go. It exists because in 2025 we paged the wrong team four times during high-severity events and lost an average of 23 minutes each time.

2. Destinations
- security_incident_response — the Security Incident Response Team (SIRT) on-call.
- database_oncall — the Data Platform on-call (owns self-managed databases: PostgreSQL clusters, Redis, and their replicas).
- platform_oncall — the Core Platform on-call (Kubernetes, networking, service mesh, application runtime, anything not owned by another destination).
- vendor_support — open a priority case with the vendor that manages the component, and create a ticket for the platform team (no page).
- no_page_ticket_only — no page; a ticket is created for the owning team's next business day.

3. Routing rules — apply in this order; the first rule that matches decides the destination
Rule 1 — Security signals. Alerts from the IDS (severity high or critical), the cloud audit anomaly detector, and the secrets scanner go to security_incident_response.
   Exception 1a: secrets-scanner findings whose fingerprint appears on the Known Test Fixtures allowlist (KTF list) are routed to no_page_ticket_only.
Rule 2 — Maintenance suppression. An alert is routed to no_page_ticket_only if ALL of the following hold: (a) the alert fires during an active maintenance window recorded in the change calendar for the component that raised it; (b) the alert type appears on that window's "expected alerts" list. A maintenance window is active only between its start and end times and only while its status in the change calendar is "Scheduled" or "In progress". A window with status "Cancelled" or "Postponed" is not active at any time.
Rule 3 — Database alerts. For self-managed database components: replica lag above 300 seconds sustained for at least 5 minutes; primary failover; disk usage above 90%; connection saturation above 95% for 10 minutes → database_oncall.
Rule 4 — Vendor-managed components. Any alert from a component marked "vendor-managed" in the component inventory → vendor_support.
Rule 5 — Default. Anything else → platform_oncall.

4. Definitions
4.1 "Component" — an entry in the component inventory (Section B below). Alerts carry the component ID in the field comp_id.
4.2 "Self-managed" — deployed and operated by Pelagos staff on Pelagos infrastructure. "Vendor-managed" — operated by a third party under a managed-service contract, even if the data belongs to Pelagos.
4.3 "Sustained" — the condition held at every evaluation in the stated period (evaluations every 30 seconds).

5. Router responsibilities
5.1 The router confirms PagerRelay's decision within 5 minutes. If PagerRelay's configuration is stale (for example a maintenance window was cancelled after PagerRelay loaded it), the router overrides PagerRelay and applies this runbook.
5.2 The router never pages more than one destination for a single alert; correlated alerts are linked in the incident tool.
5.3 Escalation: if a page is not acknowledged within 10 minutes, it escalates to the secondary of the same destination, then to the duty manager.

6. Changes in revision 5
6.1 Rule 2 now requires the window's status to be Scheduled or In progress (previously any window in the calendar suppressed alerts).
6.2 Redis moved from platform ownership to Data Platform (Rule 3).
6.3 Rule 4 clarified: vendor_support is used even when the vendor-managed component is a database.

7. Hand-over and records
7.1 At 08:00 and 20:00 UTC the router hands over to the next router with a list of open alerts, suppressed alerts and any overrides made under 5.1.
7.2 Every override of PagerRelay is recorded in the incident tool with the rule applied and a one-line reason. Overrides are reviewed weekly by the Reliability team to improve PagerRelay configuration.
7.3 Suppressed alerts remain visible in the alert console with the label "suppressed" and the window ID.

8. Paging etiquette
8.1 Pages include: alert ID, component, one-line summary, dashboard link and the rule applied.
8.2 Do not page a destination "for information". Use the #ops-fyi channel instead.
8.3 Where an alert could plausibly belong to two destinations, apply the rules in order; do not page both.

9. Known false-positive sources (informational)
- checkout-svc pod restarts during node pool rotation (Wednesdays 00:00–02:00 UTC).
- CDN origin 5xx below 1% during Fastwave certificate updates.
- Secrets-scanner findings in tests/fixtures directories; most are on the KTF list.
- Analytics replica lag warnings during the nightly reporting batch (00:30–02:30 UTC).

=== PAYMENT RELIEF POLICY PR-5 (VERSION 3, 1 FEBRUARY 2025) ===

1. Purpose
PR-5 sets the conditions under which Brackwater offers a temporary Payment Relief Plan (reduced monthly payments for up to six months, with the shortfall added to the balance) to residential mortgage customers in financial difficulty. Customers who do not qualify are still offered the standard arrears support options in policy PR-2 (payment arrangements, term extensions, referral to free debt advice). PR-5 decisions must be consistent and evidence-based; case handlers may not waive any eligibility condition.

2. Definitions
2.1 "Household" — the borrowers named on the mortgage and their spouses or partners living at the mortgaged property.
2.2 "Gross Monthly Income" — the total income of the Household before tax and deductions in a calendar month, including salary, wages, self-employed drawings, pensions and regular benefits. It excludes one-off payments: annual or discretionary bonuses, redundancy lump sums, gifts, inheritances, and tax refunds.
2.3 "Hardship Event" — a change of circumstances that reduces Household income, such as job loss, reduction of hours, illness, bereavement or relationship breakdown. The "Hardship Month" is the calendar month in which the Hardship Event occurred.
2.4 "Baseline Income" — the average Gross Monthly Income over the full calendar months immediately before the Hardship Month (the number of months is set in clause 3.1(a)).
2.5 "Current Income" — the average Gross Monthly Income over the two most recent full calendar months before the application date.
2.6 "Days Past Due" — the number of days since the oldest unpaid contractual monthly payment fell due, on the application date.
2.7 "Application date" — the date on which a complete application (form PR-5A plus evidence) is received.

3. Eligibility — all conditions must be met
3.1 (a) Qualifying hardship: Current Income is at least 25% lower than Baseline Income. Baseline Income is calculated over the 12 full calendar months before the Hardship Month.
    (b) Arrears: Days Past Due is 60 or fewer.
    (c) Frequency: no Payment Relief Plan has started in the 24 months before the application date. The 24 months are measured from the start date of the previous plan, not its end date.
    (d) Property: the mortgaged property is the Household's owner-occupied main residence. Buy-to-let and second homes are excluded.
    (e) Affordability: the reduced payment proposed by the customer is at least 50% of the contractual payment.
3.2 Where a condition is not met, the case handler records the condition and offers PR-2 options.

4. Plan terms
4.1 Maximum duration six months; review at month three.
4.2 Interest continues to accrue. The shortfall is capitalised at the end of the plan unless the customer repays it earlier.
4.3 Credit reporting: plans are reported as an "arrangement to pay" to credit reference agencies.

5. Evidence
5.1 Payslips or employer letters for each employed member of the Household covering the Baseline and Current periods; bank statements for the last three months; for self-employed customers, management accounts or bank statements.
5.2 Handlers must use gross figures from payslips. Net pay figures from bank statements are used only to check that the payslips are consistent.

6. Vulnerable customers
6.1 Customers showing signs of vulnerability are referred to the Specialist Support team, which may offer additional forbearance under policy PR-9. Referral does not change PR-5 eligibility.

7. Decisions and communication
7.1 Decisions are made within 10 business days of the application date. The customer receives a written decision explaining which conditions were met or not met.
7.2 Declined customers may ask for a review by a senior handler within 30 days; the review applies the same conditions.
7.3 Collection activity (letters, calls) is paused while an application is being assessed, but arrears continue to be reported.

8. Related policies (summary)
PR-2 Arrears support: payment arrangements of up to 12 months to clear arrears; temporary interest-only switch for up to 6 months; term extension subject to affordability; referral to free debt advice charities.
PR-9 Specialist support: additional flexibility for customers with serious illness, bereavement or domestic abuse, decided by the Specialist Support team.
PR-12 Litigation: the conditions under which Brackwater issues possession proceedings (never within 6 months of the first missed payment and never while an application under PR-5 or PR-9 is being assessed).

9. Record keeping
All calculations must be recorded in the case management system with the monthly figures used, so that the decision can be audited. Quality assurance samples 10% of decisions each month.

=== AMENDMENT PR-5/A1 (EFFECTIVE 1 JULY 2026, FOR APPLICATIONS RECEIVED FROM THAT DATE) ===
(1) In clause 3.1(a), "12 full calendar months" is replaced by "6 full calendar months".
(2) The 25% threshold and the definition of Gross Monthly Income (including the exclusion of one-off payments) are unchanged.
(3) New clause 3.1(f): customers with an active County Court claim must be referred to Litigation before a plan is offered. [Not applicable in this file — no claim issued.]

ALDERMOOR INDUSTRIES SE — PROCURE-TO-PAY MANUAL, Chapter 9 "Invoice approval routing" (rev. 2026-06)

9.1 Purpose. Every supplier invoice must be approved at the correct tier before payment. The tier depends on (a) the vendor's risk category and (b) the invoice amount in EUR, including aggregation (9.5).

9.2 Identifying the vendor. Invoices are matched to a vendor master record through the trading-name alias list (Annex A). Several vendors have similar names; match on the EXACT trading name printed on the invoice, including the legal-form suffix (AG, GmbH, Ltd …). The vendor ID from Annex A is used for every later step.

9.3 Risk category. Start with the category in the vendor master (Annex B). The category is raised to ELEVATED if either of the following is true:
    (i) the vendor's payee bank account is held in a country that is not in the EU/EEA list in Annex D;
    (ii) the vendor was onboarded less than 6 months before the invoice date.
    A vendor already rated ELEVATED stays ELEVATED. No rule lowers a category.

9.4 Currency. Non-EUR invoices are converted at the reference rate for the invoice date in Annex C. Annex C quotes the amount of FOREIGN currency per 1 EUR, so EUR amount = foreign amount ÷ rate. Round to cents.

9.5 Aggregation (anti-splitting). The amount used for routing is the current invoice PLUS all earlier invoices from the SAME vendor ID against the SAME purchase order whose invoice dates fall within the 30 calendar days before the current invoice date. Earlier invoices are converted at the rate for their own invoice date.

9.6 Approval matrix (routing amount in EUR):
| Risk category | Tier 1 Team lead | Tier 2 Department head | Tier 3 CFO           | Tier 4 Board (Finance Committee) |
|---------------|------------------|------------------------|----------------------|----------------------------------|
| STANDARD      | ≤ 10,000         | > 10,000 – 50,000      | > 50,000 – 250,000   | > 250,000                        |
| ELEVATED      | ≤ 5,000          | > 5,000 – 25,000       | > 25,000 – 100,000   | > 100,000                        |

9.7 Other rules. Capex invoices additionally need the asset register number (does not change the tier). Intercompany invoices (vendor IDs starting with IC-) are routed to Group Accounting and are out of scope of this chapter. Invoices without a PO go to the "no-PO" exception queue first.

KESTREL VALLEY COMMUNITY COLLEGE — HARDSHIP BURSARY REGULATIONS 2026/27
(Approved by the Student Finance Committee, 2026-05-12. Applies to awards for the academic year starting 2026-09-01.)

PART A — AWARD LEVELS
A.1 The bursary is paid at one of five levels:
    Level 0 — no award
    Level 1 — EUR 500
    Level 2 — EUR 1,200
    Level 3 — EUR 2,000
    Level 4 — EUR 3,000
A.2 The level is determined by the PER-CAPITA COUNTABLE INCOME of the assessed household (Part D), using the table in Part E, subject to the asset rule in Part F.

PART B — DEPENDENCY STATUS
B.1 A student is INDEPENDENT if on the reference date (1 September of the award year) at least one of the following is true:
    (a) the student is 24 years old or older;
    (b) the student is married;
    (c) the student has at least one dependent child living with them;
    (d) the student was in local-authority care after their 16th birthday.
B.2 Otherwise the student is DEPENDENT.
B.3 For all purposes of these regulations, a registered civil partnership is treated exactly like a marriage, and a registered civil partner exactly like a spouse.
B.4 Dependency status is fixed on the reference date; later changes apply only from the next award year.

PART C — ASSESSED HOUSEHOLD
C.1 Dependent students: the assessed household is the parent(s) the student normally lives with, their spouse/partner if any, the student, and all other children living in that household.
C.2 Independent students: the assessed household is the student, their spouse (if any), and their dependent children (if any). Parents' income and household are NOT assessed for independent students, even if parental data was supplied on the form.
C.3 Household size = number of persons in the assessed household.

PART D — COUNTABLE INCOME
D.1 Countable income = sum over the assessed household (excluding children under 18) of: gross employment income for the previous calendar year (2025), net self-employment profit, pensions, and taxable benefits.
D.2 Excluded from countable income: child benefit; disability-related allowances; student loans and grants; earnings from the college's WORK-STUDY programme (for any student); one-off gifts under EUR 1,000.
D.3 Dependent students only: deduct EUR 2,000 from the household's countable income for each OTHER child of the household enrolled full-time in higher education.
D.4 Per-capita countable income = countable income ÷ household size, rounded to the nearest euro.

PART E — LEVEL TABLE (per-capita countable income, EUR)
| Per-capita countable income | Level |
|-----------------------------|-------|
| up to 7,000                 | 4     |
| 7,001 – 10,500              | 3     |
| 10,501 – 14,000             | 2     |
| 14,001 – 18,000             | 1     |
| above 18,000                | 0     |

PART F — ASSETS
F.1 If the assessed household's savings and investments (excluding the main home and one car) exceed EUR 40,000, the level is capped at Level 1.
F.2 Assets are declared on the form; the college may request statements.

PART G — PROCEDURE (reference)
G.1 Applications close 2026-10-15. Late applications are assessed only if funds remain.
G.2 Evidence: P60/annual payslip or tax assessment for each income line; certificate for civil status; enrolment certificates for siblings.
G.3 Payments are made in two instalments (November, February) to the student's own account.
G.4 Students must be enrolled at least half-time on the census date (2026-10-01).
G.5 Appeals go to the Student Finance Committee within 28 days of the decision letter.
G.6 Assessors record the dependency decision, the household composition, each countable and excluded income line, and the per-capita figure on the assessment sheet, so that the decision can be checked by a second assessor.
G.7 Amounts are taken in whole euros as declared and evidenced; the college does not index 2025 income to 2026 prices.

PART H — FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
Q: I filled in my parents' details because the form asked for them. Does that matter? — A: The form collects parental data from everyone. Whether it is used depends only on Part B.
Q: My partner and I are not married but have lived together for years. — A: Cohabitation without marriage or registered civil partnership does not make a student independent.
Q: My work-study job is my main income. — A: Work-study earnings are still excluded (D.2).
Q: My sibling is at university; can I deduct that? — A: Only dependent students' households get the D.3 deduction.

PART I — WORKED EXAMPLES (illustrative, fictional students)
I.1 Dependent student, age 19, lives with mother (employment 2025: EUR 31,000) and brother (17). Household 3. Countable 31,000. Per capita 10,333 → Level 3.
I.2 Dependent student, age 21, lives with both parents (employment EUR 48,000 and EUR 12,000) and a sister (22) studying full-time at university. Household 4. Countable 60,000 − 2,000 (D.3) = 58,000. Per capita 14,500 → Level 1.
I.3 Independent student, age 26, single, no children. Employment EUR 11,400; work-study EUR 2,900 (excluded). Household 1. Per capita 11,400 → Level 2.
I.4 Independent student, age 22, married, one child aged 2. Spouse employment EUR 24,600; student no income; child benefit EUR 3,000 (excluded). Household 3. Per capita 8,200 → Level 3.
I.5 Independent student, age 30, savings EUR 52,000, income EUR 6,000. Per capita 6,000 → Level 4 by table, capped to Level 1 by F.1.

PART J — RELATED FUNDS (not assessed on this form)
J.1 Childcare Support Fund: separate application; up to EUR 1,500 per year towards registered childcare.
J.2 Travel Grant: students living more than 40 km from campus may claim 50 % of a public-transport season ticket.
J.3 Emergency Loan: interest-free, up to EUR 800, repayable within the academic year.
J.4 Receiving a hardship bursary does not affect eligibility for J.1–J.3.

PART K — DATA PROTECTION
K.1 Information supplied is used only to assess student-finance applications and is deleted 6 years after the last payment.
K.2 Parental information supplied for independent students is deleted at the end of the assessment and is not used.
K.3 Applicants may request a copy of their data at any time from the Student Finance Office.

PART L — CHANGE LOG
2026-05-12  Part E thresholds raised by approx. 5 % for inflation. D.2 extended: work-study earnings now excluded for ALL students (previously dependent students only).
2025-05-20  B.3 added (registered civil partnerships).

=====================================================================
PART 1 — RULES
=====================================================================
1.1 Credits are calculated per BILLING PERIOD. A customer's billing period runs from their billing day (inclusive) to the day before the next billing day. Only outage time inside the billing period counts; an outage crossing a boundary counts only for the part inside.
1.2 Identify the radio cell serving the customer's service address using the address-to-cell register (Part 3). Outages are logged per cell (Part 4).

1.4 Counted outages: only log entries with impact "SERVICE-AFFECTING" count. Entries with impact "DEGRADED" (slower speeds, service still available) do not count.
1.5 Planned maintenance does not count if it was announced to customers at least 48 hours before it started. Planned maintenance announced later than that counts like an unplanned outage.
1.6 Add up all counted outage time for the serving cell in the billing period (hours and minutes), then apply the credit table (Part 2).
1.7 Business plans: for plans classified as BUSINESS in the plan catalogue (Part 5), the credit percentage from Part 2 is doubled (maximum 100 %).

BRIGHTWATER OUTDOOR GMBH — PRIVACY OPERATIONS
Case pack for data subject request DSR-2026-0892 (prepared for the privacy analyst on duty)
Contents: Part 1 — Customer Data Handling Standard CDH-4, version 3.1 (in force since 1 March 2024) with Amendment 2026-1; Part 2 — CRM and ERP extracts; Part 3 — correspondence; Part 4 — Legal hold register extract.

PART 1 — CUSTOMER DATA HANDLING STANDARD CDH-4 (v3.1)

§1 Scope
1.1 CDH-4 governs how Brightwater stores, uses, restricts and erases personal data of customers of the web shop and the retail stores.
1.2 Employee data, supplier contacts and job applicants are covered by separate standards (HR-7, PRC-2, TA-3).
1.3 Where CDH-4 requires a record to be "restricted", the record is moved to the restricted archive: it is kept, but may only be accessed by Finance, Legal or Privacy for the purpose for which it is retained, and it is excluded from marketing, analytics and customer service tools.

§2 Definitions
2.1 "Customer" — a natural person with a web-shop account or a loyalty card, identified by a Customer ID in the CRM.
2.2 "Account Data" — name, contact details, login credentials, saved addresses, saved payment tokens, preferences and loyalty data.
2.3 "Order Data" — baskets, quotes, order confirmations, delivery tracking and order-related customer service notes.
2.4 "Transaction Record" — the record of a completed sale for which an invoice was issued: the invoice itself, the corresponding payment record and the delivery confirmation. Baskets, quotes, pro-forma documents and orders cancelled before an invoice was issued are not Transaction Records, even if a payment was authorised and later released. A pro-forma document is not an invoice.
2.5 "Warranty Record" — product registration and warranty claim data needed to handle a warranty claim for a product sold to the Customer.
2.6 "Marketing Data" — newsletter subscription, consent log, campaign responses, segmentation attributes.
2.7 "Legal Hold" — an instruction from Legal to preserve all data relating to a specified Customer ID (or IDs) because of actual or anticipated litigation, a regulatory inquiry or a payment dispute.
2.8 "Verified Request" — a request that meets the verification requirements of §3.
2.9 "Invoice date" — the date printed on the invoice as its date of issue. It may differ from the order date and from the delivery date.

§3 Verification of requests
3.1 A request is verified if it is (a) submitted through the privacy form while the Customer is logged into the account, or (b) sent by e-mail from the e-mail address registered on the account and confirmed by the Customer through the six-digit code sent to that address.
3.2 A request sent from any other e-mail address or by post is verified only when the requester provides two of the following that match the CRM: an order number, the billing postcode, the loyalty card number, the last four digits of a saved card.
3.3 A request made by a third party on behalf of a Customer requires a signed authority from the Customer in addition to verification under 3.1 or 3.2.
3.4 Until a request is verified, no action is taken on it other than asking for verification. The response deadline in §7 runs from the date of verification.

§4 Erasure requests
4.1 On a Verified Request for erasure, Brightwater erases all personal data relating to the Customer ID, subject only to 4.2 to 4.4.
4.2 Legal Hold. While a Legal Hold covering the Customer ID is active, nothing is erased; all data relating to that Customer ID is restricted until the hold is released, and the request is then processed under 4.1.
4.3 Transaction Records whose retention period (§5) has not ended on the day the erasure is carried out are not erased but restricted; they are erased at the end of the retention period without a further request.
4.4 Warranty Records are retained (restricted) while the warranty period for the product plus six months is running.
4.5 Marketing Data is always erased immediately; the Customer's e-mail address is added to the suppression list in hashed form so that it is not re-imported from partner lists. The hashed suppression entry is not personal data held about the Customer for the purposes of 4.1.
4.6 An erasure request is not refused because the Customer has an open balance; Finance is informed and collects on the basis of the Transaction Records.
4.7 Loyalty points lapse on erasure. The Customer is told this in the acknowledgement.

§5 Retention periods
5.1 Transaction Records: ten (10) years from the end of the calendar year in which the invoice date falls.
5.2 Warranty Records: the warranty period of the product plus six months.
5.3 Customer service tickets not related to an order: three years from closure.
5.4 CCTV images from stores: 72 hours, unless a Legal Hold applies.

§6 Legal holds
6.1 Legal Holds are entered in the Legal Hold register by Legal, identifying the Customer ID(s) covered. A hold covers only the Customer IDs listed.
6.2 A Legal Hold remains active until Legal records its release in the register. Once released, the Customer's data is handled under the normal rules; release does not revive or cancel any pending request.

§7 Response deadline
7.1 Erasure is carried out and confirmed to the Customer within 30 days of the Verified Request.
7.2 Erased data may persist in encrypted backups for up to 35 days until the backup cycle overwrites it. This is not a ground for refusing or delaying erasure.

§8 Refusal
8.1 An erasure request may only be refused if it is manifestly unfounded or excessive (e.g. repeated identical requests within 3 months), as decided by the Data Protection Officer.

§9 Business accounts
9.1 For business accounts (account type "B2B" in the CRM), contact persons' data is erased on request, but Transaction Records of the business are retained for ten (10) years from the end of the calendar year of the invoice date regardless of Amendment 2026-1, because business customers' invoices are also retained under the commercial record-keeping rules of the purchaser's contract.

§10 Access and portability requests
10.1 On a Verified Request for access, Brightwater provides a copy of all personal data relating to the Customer ID within 30 days, including restricted records, in a commonly used electronic format.
10.2 Portability exports cover Account Data and Order Data provided by the Customer; derived segmentation attributes are excluded.
10.3 An access request made together with an erasure request is answered first; erasure follows once the export has been downloaded or 14 days after it was made available, whichever is earlier.

§11 Rectification and objection
11.1 Inaccurate Account Data is corrected within 10 days of a Verified Request.
11.2 An objection to marketing is handled as a request to erase Marketing Data only (4.5 applies); other data is not affected unless the Customer also requests erasure.
11.3 Where a Customer's wording is unclear ("stop contacting me", "remove me from your lists"), Privacy asks whether erasure of the whole account is intended before acting beyond 11.2.

§12 Store purchases without account
12.1 Receipts of store purchases paid by card are Transaction Records of the store; they are linked to a Customer ID only where a loyalty card was scanned.
12.2 Store purchases with a loyalty card scan appear in the ERP under the Customer ID with document type "POS".

AMENDMENT 2026-1 TO CDH-4 (approved by the Data Protection Officer and the CFO, effective 1 January 2026)
A. §5.1 is replaced by: "Transaction Records: seven (7) years from the end of the calendar year in which the invoice date falls."
B. The new §5.1 applies to all Transaction Records held on or after 1 January 2026, including records created before that date. Records whose seven-year period ended before 1 January 2026 are to be erased in the Q1 2026 clean-up run, unless restricted for another reason.
C. §9.1 is unaffected.
D. The Q1 2026 clean-up run was completed on 27 March 2026 for all consumer accounts without an active Legal Hold on that date.

AURELLE AIR — CUSTOMER RELATIONS, COMPENSATION DESK
Claim file CR-26-08-44187. Documents: (1) Passenger Service Commitment (PSC), edition 2025, as amended by Revision 3; (2) superseded PSC Revision 2 list of extraordinary circumstances (retained in the claim template); (3) Annex D distance table extract; (4) booking and operational records; (5) claim correspondence.

(1) PASSENGER SERVICE COMMITMENT — EDITION 2025 (in force for flights from 1 April 2025), WITH REVISION 3 (in force for flights operated from 1 February 2026)

Part A — General
A1 The PSC is part of Aurelle Air's Conditions of Carriage. It gives passengers rights to care, rerouting, refunds and fixed compensation in the cases described below. It does not limit any rights passengers have under the law of the country of departure.
A2 The PSC applies to passengers holding a confirmed reservation on a flight operated by Aurelle Air, who presented themselves for check-in by the published deadline (or, with online check-in, at the gate by the boarding deadline).
A3 Codeshare flights marketed by Aurelle Air but operated by another airline are handled under the operating airline's conditions.

Part B — Definitions
B1 "Booking" — one or more flights under one booking reference (PNR), ticketed together. Flights booked under separate PNRs are separate Bookings even when the passengers travel together.
B2 "Final Destination" — the destination on the ticket of the last flight of the Booking. Alternative connecting flights taken because of a disruption do not change the Final Destination.
B3 "Arrival Time" — the moment at which at least one door of the aircraft is opened after the aircraft has reached its parking position, passengers being permitted to leave the aircraft. Touchdown time and on-block time are recorded for operational purposes and are not the Arrival Time.
B4 "Arrival Delay" — the difference between the scheduled arrival time at the Final Destination of the Booking and the Arrival Time at the Final Destination, both expressed in the same time reference.
B5 "Distance" — the great-circle distance between the airport of first departure and the Final Destination of the Booking, as listed in Annex D. For Bookings with connections, the distances of the individual flights are not added.
B6 "Extraordinary Circumstances" — the circumstances listed in Part F, which could not have been avoided even if all reasonable measures had been taken.
B7 "Rerouting" — carriage to the Final Destination under comparable conditions at the earliest opportunity, offered by Aurelle Air after a cancellation, denied boarding or missed connection.

Part C — Care
C1 Meals and refreshments in reasonable relation to the waiting time, from 2 hours of expected delay (short flights), 3 hours (medium), 4 hours (long).
C2 Hotel accommodation where an overnight stay becomes necessary.
C3 Care is provided in kind (vouchers) or reimbursed against receipts within reasonable limits.
C4 Passengers are offered two telephone calls or e-mails free of charge.
C5 Care is not refused because the cause of the delay is an Extraordinary Circumstance; E3 limits fixed compensation only.

Part D — Refunds and rerouting
D1 Where a flight is cancelled, or a delay of 5 hours or more is expected, passengers may choose a refund of the unused part of the ticket instead of travel.
D2 A passenger who misses a connection within the same Booking because of a delay of an earlier flight is offered Rerouting.

Part E — Fixed compensation
E1 A passenger whose Arrival Delay at the Final Destination is 3 hours or more receives fixed compensation according to the Distance:
  Distance up to 1,500 km: EUR 250
  Distance more than 1,500 km and up to 3,500 km: EUR 400
  Distance more than 3,500 km: EUR 300 if the Arrival Delay is 3 hours or more but less than 4 hours; EUR 600 if the Arrival Delay is 4 hours or more.
E2 Compensation under E1 is reduced by 50 % where the passenger was offered Rerouting and the Arrival Delay at the Final Destination does not exceed: 2 hours (Distance up to 1,500 km), 3 hours (more than 1,500 up to 3,500 km), 4 hours (more than 3,500 km).
E3 No compensation is payable where the delay or cancellation was caused by Extraordinary Circumstances, or where the passenger was informed of a cancellation at least 14 days before scheduled departure.
E4 Compensation is paid per passenger, in cash, bank transfer or (with the passenger's written agreement) travel vouchers. Infants travelling free of charge on a lap are not entitled to compensation.
E5 Where a delay on an earlier flight of the Booking causes a missed connection, the Arrival Delay at the Final Destination is decisive; the cause of the delay of the earlier flight is examined under E3.
E6 Claims must be made within 2 years of the scheduled date of the flight.

Part F — Extraordinary Circumstances (as amended by Revision 3)
F1 Meteorological conditions incompatible with the safe operation of the flight.
F2 Air traffic management decisions (slot restrictions, airspace closures) and strikes by staff not employed by Aurelle Air or its contractors.
F3 Security risks, political instability, and airport closures ordered by authorities.
F4 Bird strikes and damage to the aircraft caused by third parties (e.g. ground-handling vehicles of other operators).
F5 Hidden manufacturing defects that affect the safety of the flight and that the aircraft manufacturer or an authority has notified to operators.
F6 Revision 3 note: technical problems that arise in connection with the maintenance or operation of the aircraft, including those discovered during routine checks or pre-flight inspections, are not Extraordinary Circumstances unless covered by F5. Staff shortages and strikes by Aurelle Air's own staff are not Extraordinary Circumstances.

Part G — Downgrading
G1 Passengers placed in a lower class than booked receive a refund of 30 % (up to 1,500 km), 50 % (1,500–3,500 km) or 75 % (above 3,500 km) of the ticket price of the affected flight.

Part H — Baggage
H1 Delayed checked baggage: reimbursement of reasonable essential purchases up to EUR 50 per day for up to 5 days, against receipts.
H2 Lost baggage: liability as set out in the Conditions of Carriage, Article 17; claims within 21 days of the date the baggage should have been delivered.
H3 Baggage delays do not give rise to fixed compensation under Part E.

Part I — Claims handling
I1 Claims are assessed per passenger. A claim form may cover several passengers of one Booking; passengers on other Bookings must claim separately.

(1) ACADEMIC APPEALS REGULATIONS, 2025/26 EDITION

Section 1 — Interpretation
1.1 These Regulations apply to appeals against decisions of Boards of Examiners and of Progression Boards on taught programmes.
1.2 "Student" includes a person whose registration ended within the previous six months.
1.3 "Result" means a decision of a Board of Examiners or Progression Board recorded on the student record: a module mark, a progression decision, or an award and classification decision.
1.4 "Working day" means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays in England and the University closure days listed in the Academic Calendar. Days on which teaching does not take place (reading weeks, vacations) are working days unless they are closure days.
1.5 "Publication" of a Result means its release to the student on the Student Portal. E-mail notifications that a Result is available are courtesy messages and do not affect the date of Publication.
1.6 Periods expressed in working days run from the working day following the event that starts them. A period ends at 23:59 UK time on its last working day.
1.7 "Lodged" means received through the Appeals form (AP1) on the Student Portal. Where the Student Portal is unavailable for more than four hours on the last day of a period, an appeal e-mailed to appeals@harwood-met.example on that day is treated as lodged.

Section 2 — Who may appeal
2.1 Any Student may appeal against a Result that affects them.
2.2 An appeal may not be made by a third party except with the student's written consent.
2.3 A student who has attended a graduation ceremony and accepted the award to which the appeal relates may not appeal against the classification of that award.

Section 3 — Time limits
3.1 An appeal must be lodged within 10 working days of Publication of the Result.
3.2 An appeal lodged out of time is not admissible unless the student shows, with independent evidence, that they were prevented from lodging it in time by circumstances beyond their control; in that case it must be lodged within 5 working days after those circumstances ended.
3.3 Time limits are not extended because a student is awaiting the outcome of an informal discussion, a request for feedback or a request for a re-count of marks, unless the Appeals Office agreed an extension in writing before the time limit expired.

Section 4 — Grounds
4.1 An appeal may be made only on one or more of the following grounds:
  (a) a material procedural irregularity in the conduct of the assessment or of the Board's decision, which may have affected the Result;
  (b) circumstances affecting the student's performance which, for good reason, the student was unable to disclose before the Board met;
  (c) evidence of prejudice or bias, or of a reasonable perception of bias, on the part of an examiner.
4.2 Disagreement with the academic judgement of examiners is not a ground of appeal. Academic judgement includes the marks awarded, the assessment of the quality of work and the application of marking criteria.
4.3 An appeal which includes matters outside 4.1 is admissible in respect of those grounds that fall within 4.1; the other matters are struck out at screening.
4.4 An appeal consisting only of matters outside 4.1 is not admissible.

Section 5 — Stage 1 (informal resolution)
5.1 Before lodging an appeal, a student must first raise the matter with the Programme Leader (Stage 1) and allow five working days for a response. The Stage 1 outcome or the expiry of five working days without a response must be recorded on the AP1 form.
5.2 Stage 1 does not apply where the appeal is against an award and classification decision of a Board of Examiners, or where the matter concerns the conduct of the Programme Leader.
5.3 Raising a matter under Stage 1 does not stop the time limit in Section 3 running.

Section 6 — Evidence
6.1 Documentary evidence should accompany the AP1 form. Evidence not available when the appeal is lodged may be submitted within 10 working days after lodging.
6.2 Medical evidence must be from a registered practitioner and must cover the relevant dates.

Section 7 — Screening and outcomes
7.1 The Appeals Office screens each appeal for admissibility (Sections 2–5) within 10 working days of lodging.
7.2 Admissible appeals are referred to an Appeals Panel. Inadmissible appeals receive a Completion of Procedures letter.

Section 8 — Appeals Panel
8.1 An Appeals Panel consists of a chair from the Senate, an academic from another faculty and, where the student requests it, a student member nominated by the Students' Union.
8.2 The Panel considers the written submission, the evidence and the response of the Board of Examiners. The student may attend and be accompanied by a friend or a Students' Union adviser.
8.3 The Panel may (a) dismiss the appeal; (b) refer the matter back to the Board of Examiners for reconsideration, with directions; (c) where the ground in 4.1(a) is upheld, direct that the student be offered a further attempt at the affected assessment without penalty.
8.4 The Panel does not substitute its own academic judgement for that of the examiners.

Section 9 — Completion of procedures
9.1 A Completion of Procedures letter is issued at the end of the internal process. The student may then take the matter to the independent external reviewer within 12 months.
9.2 A student whose appeal is found inadmissible at screening may ask the Pro-Vice-Chancellor (Education) to review the screening decision within 5 working days of the decision.

Section 10 — Records and confidentiality
10.1 Appeal files are retained for six years after the Completion of Procedures letter.
10.2 Information provided in an appeal is shared only with those who need it to consider the appeal.

Section 11 — Appeals against progression decisions (Progression Boards)
11.1 A student required to resit or repeat may appeal under these Regulations. Stage 1 applies to all progression appeals.
11.2 A progression appeal does not suspend the resit; the student should sit the resit while the appeal is pending.
11.3 For progression decisions made in the summer cycle, the time limit in 3.1 is 10 working days irrespective of any amendment, because resit arrangements begin in August.
